audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Ryze Level 1 and Level 6 and Jax the two-item stage, while whys[6] says the two-item Ryze loop is what Jax cannot answer.
audit.why: Packet chart and the audited Jax-side mirror both read Skill / Jax x5 / Ryze; the packet's flagged defect is the stored chart, not the packet's.
audit.corrected: Skill / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Ryze, ratings inverted from the mirror's, as matched pairs across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was scored as a Ryze stage.
audit.why: Grandmaster-at-Arms rewards the extended trade Jax forces with Leap Strike (8s at rank 1, 700 range) once Rune Prison is down, and Realm Warp adds no damage to end that fight faster. Ryze's stage is two items.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten as Jax's; two items flipped to Ryze.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says four times that Counter Strike dodges Ryze's 'empowered Q autos' and treats the dodge as the reason not to commit.
audit.why: Riot's text: Jax dodges all incoming ATTACKS for a short duration, then counterattacks and stuns. Ryze's damage is Overload and Spell Flux — spells, not attacks — so the dodge does nothing to his rotation. The thing to wait out is the stun, on 17/15/13/11/9. Empower is a 7/6/5/4/3 auto-attack reset, so the wind-up rather than a cast is the step-back tell. Level 1 also does not require walking to melee: Overload is 1000 range and Spell Flux 615.
audit.corrected: Dodge scoped to basic attacks, the stun named as the real gate with its 17s rank-1 cooldown, the Empower reset added, and the melee walk-up removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called 'Grandmaster's Might' throughout both layers.
audit.why: Riot's data gives the ability name as Grandmaster-at-Arms; 'Grandmaster at Arms' is also his title, which is how the wrong form crept in.
audit.corrected: Renamed in the strings I touched.

edits.before: W root threatens jungle follow-up, but it's also your kite tool — spending it greedily is how you die.
edits.after: Counter Strike is up: its stun ends your combo, while the dodge does nothing to your spells.

edits.before: Realm Warp opens flanks and escapes, and your EQ DPS now duels most tops on their cooldown gaps.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms wins the long trade he forces; Realm Warp adds no damage to end it.

edits.before: Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1; the dodge misses your spells, so only the stun times your commit.

edits.before: Track Jax’s Counter Strike: Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Counter Strike (17s at rank 1): it dodges basic attacks, not your spells — wait out the stun, not the dodge.

edits.before: That’s Jax’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Empower is an auto reset — the wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to step back.

edits.before: Counter Strike (E) is now active and dodges your empowered Q autos, then stuns you inside the Rune Prison window — Jax wins every contested trade from this point.
edits.after: Counter Strike is active: the dodge ignores your spells, but its stun lands inside your Rune Prison window, and Jax wins every contested trade from here.

edits.before: Grandmaster's Might passive adds bonus stats at the end of extended trades, and Jax can force extension by Leap Striking after your root expires; Realm Warp has no damage to end the fight faster.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms adds bonus stats at the end of extended trades, and Jax forces that extension with Leap Strike the moment your root expires; Realm Warp has no damage to end the fight faster.

edits.before: Activate Counter Strike (E) the moment you step into melee range to dodge your empowered Q autos and stun mid-combo
edits.after: Activate Counter Strike as you commit so its stun interrupts your rotation mid-combo and flips the trade back

edits.before: Stack Trinity Force then force extended trades where Grandmaster's Might passive adds bonus attack damage and attack speed
edits.after: Stack Trinity Force then force extended trades where Grandmaster-at-Arms adds bonus attack damage and attack speed

edits.before: At level 1 you and Jax are both feeling each other out — you have only Q and must walk into melee range to do anything meaningful, while Jax can hold Counter Strike and stun you for auto-trading. Neither of you can punish cleanly so farm passively and establish where the wave settles. The moment Jax hits level 2 and has Counter Strike available, every trade you attempt risks a stun on your W-root timing — he can E the moment you step up to cast Spell Flux, eat your autos through the dodge, then stun you while Rune Prison's empowered Q is still cycling. At level 3 your full E-Q-W loop is online, but you must bait Counter Strike on a creep or a fake step-up before you commit the W-root; if he has E ready when you root him, he stuns you inside your own combo and the exchange flips.
edits.after: At level 1 you and Jax are both feeling each other out — Overload reaches 1000 and Spell Flux 615, so you never need melee range, while Jax has nothing that reaches you first. Neither of you can punish cleanly, so farm and establish where the wave settles. The moment Jax hits level 2 and has Counter Strike available, every trade risks a stun on your W-root timing — the dodge does not touch your spells, but he can E as you step up and stun you while your empowered Q is still cycling. At level 3 your full E-Q-W loop is online, but bait Counter Strike on a creep or a fake step-up before you commit the root; if it is up when you root him, he stuns you inside your own combo and the exchange flips.

notes: Main correction: Counter Strike dodges basic ATTACKS, not abilities — Ryze's damage is spells, so the dodge half of Jax's E is irrelevant to this matchup and the page was building its whole trade rule on it. What actually gates the commit is the stun, 17s at rank 1. Also fixed the ultimate's name (Grandmaster-at-Arms, not Grandmaster's Might) where I touched the string; the same wrong name remains in the full layer's untouched copies and in the 'mid' paragraph. Separately, spikes[] are out of order: spikes[1].when is '1st item' while spikes[2].when is 'Lvl 3'. Both are under 25 characters so the applier skips them — needs a direct swap.
